Plot a Sample Correlation Heatmap

plot_correlation_heatmap.Rd

Creates a heatmap of pairwise sample correlations, calculated via the Spearman method. The function includes a "smart sorting" feature to correctly order axes based on numeric parts of labels (e.g., "Day1", "Day2", "Day10").

Usage

plot_correlation_heatmap(PD, order_by = NULL, label_by = NULL)

Arguments

PD

A ProtData object.

order_by

Optional. A character string specifying a column in the condition slot by which to order the samples on the heatmap axes. If the column contains numeric parts, a natural sort is applied.

label_by

Optional. A character string specifying a column in the condition slot to use for relabeling the heatmap axes.

Value

A ggplot object representing the heatmap.

Examples

# Create sample data with timepoints for sorting
raw_data <- data.frame(
  Gene = paste0("G", 1:5),
  Sample_D10 = rnorm(5, 15), # Treatment
  Sample_D1 = rnorm(5, 10),  # Control
  Sample_D2 = rnorm(5, 10)   # Control
)
cond_df <- data.frame(
  SampleID = c("Sample_D1", "Sample_D2", "Sample_D10"),
  Timepoint = c("Day1", "Day2", "Day10"),
  Group = c("Control", "Control", "Treatment")
)
pd_obj <- create_protdata(dat = raw_data, condition = cond_df)

# Example 1: Default alphanumeric sorting (D1, D10, D2)
p1 <- plot_correlation_heatmap(pd_obj)
#> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
#> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.
#> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the ProtPipe package.
#>   Please report the issue to the authors.
if (interactive()) print(p1)

# Example 2: Smart sorting by 'Timepoint' (D1, D2, D10)
p2 <- plot_correlation_heatmap(pd_obj, order_by = "Timepoint")
#> Numeric values detected in ordering variable. Applying natural sort.
if (interactive()) print(p2)

# Example 3: Smart sorting and relabeling by 'Group'
p3 <- plot_correlation_heatmap(pd_obj, order_by = "Timepoint", label_by = "Group")
#> Numeric values detected in ordering variable. Applying natural sort.
if (interactive()) print(p3)
